sentences.text:
This bail application has been filed by the applicant Nitin seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 528 of 2022, under Sections 498A/34, 304-B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S.
Kanchala, District Shamli, during the pendency of trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: At the very outset, the learned A.G.A. contends that the applicant is husband of the deceased.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: As per the post mortem report of the deceased, the cause of death of deceased is asphyxia as a result of ante mortem strangulation.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
He,
however, submits that even though applicant is a named as well as charge sheeted accused, yet, he is liable to be enlarged on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
He submits that trial has already commenced and four prosecution witnesses namely P.W. 1 Chentan Panchal, first informant/brother of the deceased, P.W.2 Poonam,
mother of the deceased, P.W. 3 Devendra father of the deceased and P.W. 5 Ankit Panchal, brother of the deceased have already deposed before Court below, but they have not supported the prosecution story.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: At this stage, the Court raised a pointed query as to whether charge under Section 302 IPC has been altered or not.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant could not reply the same.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Considering the above and also the fact that the death of the deceased has occurred in her marital home, cause of the death of the deceased is asphyxia as a result of ante mortem strangulation and in view of the statements of P.W. 1, P.W. 2, P.W. 3 and P.W. 5, the charge will have to be altered under Section 302 IPC, no good ground exists to enlarge the applicant on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: As a result, present bail application fails and is liable to be rejected.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is, accordingly, rejected.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023.json

"Heard Mr. Ramendra Gupta, the learned counsel for the applicant and the learned A.G.A. for the State.

sentences.text: This bail application has been filed by the applicant Nitin seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 528 of 2022, under Sections 498A/34, 304-B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Kanchala, District Shamli, during the pendency of trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: At the very outset, the learned A.G.A. contends that the applicant is husband of the deceased.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: As per the post mortem report of the deceased, the cause of death of deceased is asphyxia as a result of ante mortem strangulation.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: He, however, submits that even though applicant is a named as well as charge sheeted accused, yet, he is liable to be enlarged on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: He submits that trial has already commenced and four prosecution witnesses namely P.W. 1 Chentan Panchal, first informant/brother of the deceased, P.W.2 Poonam, mother of the deceased, P.W. 3 Devendra father of the deceased and P.W. 5 Ankit Panchal, brother of the deceased have already deposed before Court below, but they have not supported the prosecution story.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: At this stage, the Court raised a pointed query as to whether charge under Section 302 IPC has been altered or not.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant could not reply the same.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Considering the above and also the fact that the death of the deceased has occurred in her marital home, cause of the death of the deceased is asphyxia as a result of ante mortem strangulation and in view of the statements of P.W. 1, P.W. 2, P.W. 3 and P.W. 5, the charge will have to be altered under Section 302 IPC, no good ground exists to enlarge the applicant on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: As a result, present bail application fails and is liable to be rejected.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text:
It is, accordingly, rejected."
5.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant contends that prosecution witnesses of fact who have deposed before court below have not supported the F.I.R.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: The doctor who conducted autopsy on the body of the deceased has deposed before court below as PW8.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: However, autopsy surgeon in his deposition before court below has not given any categorical opinion with regard to the cause of death of the deceased.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: On the above premise, it is thus urged that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: 6. Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch as, he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Applicant is in jail since 14.12.2022.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: As such, he has undergone more than 2 and 1/2 months of incarceration.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text:
The police report in terms of Section 173(2) Cr.P.C.
has already been submitted.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text:
As such, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168199905/
2 against applicant stands crystallized.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: However, up to this stage, no such circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: On the above premise, it is thus urged that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.

sentences.text:
In case, the applicant is enlarged on bail,
he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: 7. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: He submits that since applicant is husband of the deceased, a named and charge sheeted accused, therefore, he does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: He further submits since the occurrence giving rise to present criminal proceedings has occurred in the house of applicant, therefore, there is no eye-witness of the occurrence in question.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Therefore, even if the prosecution witnesses of fact have turned hostile, the same shall not be a ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: The trial is at an advanced stage and eight prosecution witnesses have been examined.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: As per the post-mortem of the deceased the cause of death of the deceased is strangulation.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Admittedly, the deceased is the wife of the applicant and the occurrence had taken place in the house of the applicant, since, the applicant is an inmate of the house the occurrence occurred therefore prima facie the burden is upon the applicant himself to explain the manner of occurrence in terms of Section 106 of the Evidence Act.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Furthermore, in case the prosecution witnesses have turned hostile, then the charge is liable to be awarded under Section 302 I.P.C.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: On the above conspectus, learned A.G.A. submits that no new or good ground has made out to enlarge the applicant on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Consequently, this repeat application for bail is liable to be rejected.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: 8. When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text:
9. Having heard, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of record, evidence, nature and gravity of offence, accusations made, complicity of applicant coupled with the fact that trial is at an advanced stage, as such, number of eight prosecution witnesses of fact have already been examined, as per the opinion of autopsy surgeon, the cause of death of the deceased is strangulation, the statement of the doctor who has deposed before court below is not required to be evaluated by this Court inasmuch as dictates of prudence requires that the evidence which has emerged during course of trial should not be evaluated by trial court even if it is a higher court as any observations made by this Court may hamper the prosecution or the defence, in view of above and considering the nature and gracity of offence, therefore, irrespective of the varied submissions urged in support of the present application for bail by the learned counsel for applicant,
but without making any comments on the merits of the case, this Court does not find any new or good ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.
10.
sentences._hearing_file: Nitin vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: In view of above, the bail application fails and is liable to be rejected.

sentences.text: 11. It is accordingly rejected.

6. Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch as, he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
As such, he has undergone more than 2 and 1/2 months of incarceration.
In case, the applicant is enlarged on bail,
he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
Therefore, even if the prosecution witnesses of fact have turned hostile, the same shall not be a ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.
The trial is at an advanced stage and eight prosecution witnesses have been examined.
As per the post-mortem of the deceased the cause of death of the deceased is strangulation.
Admittedly, the deceased is the wife of the applicant and the occurrence had taken place in the house of the applicant, since, the applicant is an inmate of the house the occurrence occurred therefore prima facie the burden is upon the applicant himself to explain the manner of occurrence in terms of Section 106 of the Evidence Act.
Furthermore, in case the prosecution witnesses have turned hostile, then the charge is liable to be awarded under Section 302 I.P.C.
opennyai_summary.15_February_2024__arguments:

He further submits since the occurrence giving rise to present criminal proceedings has occurred in the house of applicant, therefore, there is no eye-witness of the occurrence in question.
9. Having heard, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of record, evidence, nature and gravity of offence, accusations made, complicity of applicant coupled with the fact that trial is at an advanced stage, as such, number of eight prosecution witnesses of fact have already been examined, as per the opinion of autopsy surgeon, the cause of death of the deceased is strangulation, the statement of the doctor who has deposed before court below is not required to be evaluated by this Court inasmuch as dictates of prudence requires that the evidence which has emerged during course of trial should not be evaluated by trial court even if it is a higher court as any observations made by this Court may hamper the prosecution or the defence, in view of above and considering the nature and gracity of offence, therefore, irrespective of the varied submissions urged in support of the present application for bail by the learned counsel for applicant,
but without making any comments on the merits of the case, this Court does not find any new or good ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.
